newsitem.title: UK: Gold demand down two pct in third qtr - WGC.
newsitem.headline: Gold demand down two pct in third qtr - WGC.

text.p: Gold demand in markets monitored by the World Gold Council (WGC) totalled 655 tonnes during the 1996 third quarter, just two percent off the record 668 tonnes recorded in the same period last year, the WGC said.
Demand in the developing countries of Asia, the Middle East and Latin America set a new third quarter record.
In the developed markets total demand was seven percent down on the 1995 third quarter due to a pull back in investment demand but jewellery demand was one percent higher.
"Gold demand during the first three quarters of 1996 continued to consolidate close to last year's record levels," said George Milling-Stanley, WGC manager of gold market analysis.

The WGC is backed by a number of gold producers and monitors gold demand in countries accounting for about 75 percent of world gold consumption. The outlook for the rest of 1996 was for further consolidation at high levels of consumption as the peak demand season is still to come in both East and West, the WGC said.
